messages:
Anya: Quick sync — planning the priming strategy for the v2.3 runtime rollout. Need to pick between gradual ramp (seeders) vs burst priming (large synthetic blast) and consider kernel selection + batching effects.

Kevin: Agree. Ramp feels safer for latency SLOs but might not reach high hit-rates before GA. Burst gets fast hit-rate but risks tail latency spikes.

Jamie: Data point: in last trial when we fired a 2h synthetic blast we saw prefix hit-rate go from 8% -> 52% within 15m, but p99 latency on small models spiked ~120ms for ~10m.

Evan: Do we have a breakdown by kernel selection path? My suspicion: the burst drove different kernel choices (FP16 vs INT8 codepath) because sequence length distribution changed. Kernel warmup cost + JIT-ish selection could be contributing.

Anya: Good call. I pulled profiling from the 2h blast:
```
# simplified trace counts
kernel_switches: +1.9k
kv_cache_misses: -
kv_cache_inserts: +43k
batch_size_90pct: 18 -> 120
p99_latency_ms: 85 -> 205 (during peak)
```
Looks like heavy batching + kernel switch noise.

Kevin: If kernel selection gets toggled under load, we should avoid a sudden distribution shift. That argues for ramped seeders that mimic production prefix distribution.

Jamie: But our ramp job used uniform synthetic prefixes; the distribution mismatch could explain why hit-rate improvement plateaued at ~30% for ramp tests. Synthetic realism matters.

Maria: Can we do a hybrid: scheduled small daily synthetic jobs keyed to high-frequency prefixes + deploy-time seeders for recently changed prompts? Also autoscale-triggered priming when new instances start.

InfraBot: FYI: autoscale hook available in prod via `/hooks/prewarm-instance` — it can accept a list of prefix hashes to request.

Evan: Nice. Question on keying: we currently key cache by (model, normalized_prefix, tokenizer_version). That normalization strips whitespace and lowercases. However some customers use casing semantically. We should make keying pluggable per model.

Anya: Action: audit models for sensitive-casing cases. For v2.3 rollout, default remains lenient normalization but enable opt-in strict mode.

Kevin: Hit-rate numbers from last 7-day traffic (prod): overall 27% prefix hit-rate, top 500 prefixes account for 46% of hits. So targeting top prefixes is high ROI.

Jamie: Suggestion: make a daily job that computes top-K prefixes per region + per model and push to prewarm lists. Cron can run at 0400 UTC to avoid peak.

Evan: Need to consider privacy: compute top-K from hashed prefix signatures, not raw text. We already have tooling for differential retention.

Anya: Regarding synthetic vs live: one regression we hit earlier — synthetic sequences often had shorter tails, so KV cache TTL was tuned wrong and we evicted useful entries. Observed underwarm after 36h traffic. Should we increase default TTL and use eviction pressure signals?

Maria: TTL bump helps but increases mem usage. Better: adaptive TTL: keep longer for prefixes with repeated hits/weight. We can track sliding-window hit counts and promote keys.

Kevin: Concerning deploy-time behavior: proposal: 3-stage priming pipeline
- Stage A (immediate): seed top-200 hot prefixes from last-24h within 60s of deploy to new instances. small controlled burst.
- Stage B (ramp): 30m gradual synthetic traffic shaped to mimic real prefix length distribution and top-K weights.
- Stage C (steady): daily cron that refreshes top prefixes and runs small seeded requests.

Jamie: Sounds good. For Stage A we must throttle to avoid kernel switching. Maybe perform sequential requests with short gaps (50-100ms) instead of concurrent blast.

Evan: Also important: batching heuristics. We should bias the seeder client to produce realistic inter-arrival times to keep batching behavior similar to prod. For example, generate poisson arrivals with lambda tuned per model.

InfraBot: Note: deploy pipeline can attach a `prewarm-plan.json` blob to deploy metadata. See docs: `/docs/deploys#prewarm-plans`.

Anya: Perf regression from prior rollout: a seeder used wrong tokenizer_version and produced keys that never matched runtime normalization -> zero hit improvement and wasted cycles. Must version-lock tokenizers in seeder artifacts.

Maria: I'll add a CI check: seeder artifact must include tokenizer hash and model version; deploy will fail prewarm if mismatch.

Kevin: Measurement plan for rollout:
- baseline capture: 24h pre-deploy hit-rate and p99 latency per model/region
- during deploy: record hit-rate, kv insert/evict rates, kernel_switch count every 1m
- post-deploy: 72h comparison and A/B against canary cluster

Jamie: Can we get a small dashboard tile for this? I can wire a Grafana panel: `prefix_hit_rate`, `kv_cache_size`, `kv_evictions`, `kernel_switches`, `p99_latency`.

Evan: One more regression note: synthetic traffic caused longer KV cache write-path latency due to lock contention in our cache sharding — saw tail spikes. We should profile lock contention and maybe increase shards for heavy models.

Anya: OK owners: Maria = CI + seeder artifact locking; Jamie = Grafana panel + prewarm schedule; Evan = kernel/batching analysis + shard tuning; Kevin = rollout plan + top-K selection algo. I'll draft RFC and run a quick tabletop with SRE before we roll.

DeployBot: CID 8932: v2.3 deploy scheduled for 2026-04-02T03:00Z; prewarm pipeline enabled (prewarm-plan attached).

Anya: Thanks all. Next sync after RFC comments. :rocket:
